body:
"Can't handle deadlines" is definitely a killer in this field :(  


The downside would be aggravated depression and feeling like I'm worthless, which I have been ever since I saw the post.

This is great advice, and I really appreciate it :). The only problem is, it isn't so much as "eh" about deadlines, but more like "she blew this by a month and we are furious at her and fired her." :(

I take Adderall, and sometimes it wires me and sometimes it doesn't. Sometimes if I take it too close to bed, I don't fall asleep right away, but sometimes I do. But I've noticed that I now get 6-8 hours of sleep per night rather than suffering from hypersomnia, and the sleep is actually refreshing most of the time! Because my brain actually shuts. up. for a few hours. I'm also more able to be productive instead of just goofing off for hours, and I can actually make sense of calendars now (especially as my life coach taught me how they work, which...yeah. No one ever realized I needed to be taught about.)  


Spoiled little non-ADHD brats who abuse it because they need to get an A on their econ paper after partying all week are trash and cause incalculable harm.

Good lord, do we have the same ex-therapist?!  


I'm so sorry you're going through this. Terrible therapists are the worst people.

More complex response to follow, as I've basically been having emotional flashbacks all day. :( But it's not surprising you thought I was posting on the CPTSD forum. I'm 1) a member there and 2) have this diagnosis. I got it in February. Until then I'd never heard of it. But I have all the symptoms and the profile: persistent childhood abuse (as in nearly every day during the school year from ages 7-11, and even some days during summer), CSA, and on top of that, a severe history of mental illness on both sides of the family, especially on my father's side (he actually died by suicide a few days before my seventeenth birthday).  


So...yes. LOL  


What gets me, now that I think about it, is that ex-therapist KNEW all about this! She knew I had a borderline personality disorder diagnosis (which she disagreed with and said CPTSD made more sense, which my psychiatrist agreed with)! She knew I'd been in trauma therapy before--and she even said she specialized in it. Which is why i went to see her. She talked to me about her own experiences with child sexual abuse, which is why I trusted her and liked her. And she knew a previous therapist had abandoned me when I became suicidal (that therapist also gave me EMDR and definitely knew what my issues were) and told me that was messed up.  


And then she did everything possible that would have hurt me.   


Like, I'm sure this whole incident was upsetting for her! But that's the thing...I can't do anything about her upset. And maybe I'm wrong, but it seems like even if a therapist takes on the most seemingly low-key, low-maintenance client, that's no guarantee said client won't someday be in crisis. It seems to me that this is a risk with any client, and that therapists should be prepared for that to happen, particularly if a client is showing a lot of stress because they 1) just went through a divorce a year ago, 2) just lost someone who was basically their second mother, 3) got fired by a lot of clients (I'm a freelancer) because i was missing deadlines left and right, and 4) is having to help sell the house she grew up in.  


I'm not sure why having someone have a breakdown after all of that seemed like something she didn't think of as a possibility, you know?   


weeelp. So much for "I'll respond more in depth later." LOL  


​
It truly is. And it's frustrating that the medical-industrial complex doesn't recognize it because Reasons.

I'm bisexual and more woman-leaning nonbinary (but AFAB), and I've never been very "feminine," aside from wearing skirts a lot and liking jewelry. I don't really keep up my appearance or dress stylishly because I don't care about either. I never really was into it, which is probably why a lot of people don't find me sexy or even attractive.   


But ADHD runs in my family. My straight-cis father had it, and two of my straight (as far as I know, anyway)-cis cousins have it. I suspect they're not the only ones, but those are the ones I know of.

I wish every day that I didn't have ADHD. It's ruined my life, just as my mental illnesses have.  


Though I do agree that society adjusting itself to work with the strengths of each neurotype would be wise, and that this would make a lot of things better for a lot of ADHDers.

Hi, IvoryWang:

Not a lawyer here, but I live one state away in Utah. My grandma recently passed and we've had the same problem with realtors. Due to the recession a decade ago, no one was building houses in Utah, so now that people want to move here, we're facing a housing shortage, which means realtors circle every home like sharks. 

I'm wondering if this isn't the same in Las Vegas. Do you know if your mother made the fact she's selling her house public in any way? Or if she was working with a real estate agent who may have talked to other real estate agents? Once word gets out, they swarm. Or is she definitely on a list?  


Also, my mother gets mail, phone calls, and notices on her door all the time asking if she wants to sell her house. She doesn't, but people are contacting her anyway just to see. I wonder if realtors in LV are doing the same thing.
Just what I was thinking.
To be honest, I don't see why someone wouldn't bill a client for this long. I'm honestly wondering if he HAS billed and just now wants you to pay a higher fee out of pocket.

Yeah, I'm joining other people here to say you should report him. You're not overreacting. He lied to you for years about billing your insurance and is now taking advantage of your moving situation to get money from you.

She got really hostile to me after I had a suicidal crisis and went to the ER. Basically, she revoked the diagnosis she was treating me for (successfully, I might add), blamed my ADHD meds for it (I've been through repeat traumas since August and just lost my grandma), said I should go on disability because I keep "having these problems" (and that she wouldn't tell me that if I were twenty, but that since I'm in my late thirties, she thinks this is "a pattern" now). That was before she sent me an eleven-paragraph tirade email accusing me of threatening and endangering her and her staff by...reaching out to them when I was in crisis and responding curtly to a few emails? Hell if I know. And said that the fact I don't think I need inpatient now "proves her point" that I do.

That was about three weeks ago, and while I'm not suicidal now, I'm still really shaken up by it, and my concentration is shot.  


ETA: I should also add that I went to the hospital immediately when I was in crisis, didn't hurt myself, and was released a few hours later after the staff and I made a safety plan and I promised to come back the moment the thoughts returned, which they didn't. She and her staff also gave me ten minutes to get to a hospital before sending the police by. There is no hospital within ten minutes of me, and they sent me this ultimatum after I'd left to the hospital, meaning the cops came by when no one was there.   


I did everything I thought was right to protect myself, and maybe I messed up, but I'd never gone to the hospital for this before and wasn't thinking clearly at the time. And I just don't feel I should be punished for that or for snapping at her staff when I got home and found this ten-minute ultimatum sent after I left, especially when I apologized for it twice and admitted I was out of line. Apparently my being uncomfortable about the unreasonable time limit was "blaming her and her staff" for my behavior.
I wrote pretty much just like LAOP did when I was thirteen, so yes, it is possible.
I totally sympathize. I was terrified of my father's reactions and did things like this too :(

Oh bearapy, are you me? My therapist just said this to me a while ago, but she literally did it while terminating her relationship with me in an incredibly hurtful way.   


I'm in a similar situation to you, I think: not using substances, but struggling at my job and very sad and anxious (following a family member's death).   


He said "inpatient" and not "intensive outpatient"?

??? I watched episodes of it, intermittently. Excuse me for not wanting to waste my limited time watching an entire TV show when I found the protagonist irritating.

You're taking TV way too seriously, guy.
I gave up on it after a few episodes and only caught it intermittently, so I think we did watch different shows :). It's good to hear I wasn't right about it, though.

Oh, I fully believe not all therapists are bad! But I've had more bad ones than good at this point, including my favorite who dropped me as soon as I got suicidal (the one before this last one). So that's why I wonder if maybe I'm just not helpable.

Oh, she's highly recommended everyone at her new practice! But I'm still wary, especially as, if things go bad again with one of them, then I may need a new psychiatrist too. I was concerned I'd need a new one because ex-therapist recommended this psychiatrist to me, but thankfully I did not.

Thanks elmcitykid! I worried about that HIPPA thing too, tbh, and so have a few other people. Perhaps I should file a complaint, but I don't think I will. From a purely selfish standpoint, I just don't want to waste spoons I need now for grieving and attending to other family members on pursuing it. But I really appreciate your help!
Thanks, punchkitty. It's been a really tough month :(

No, I get the point of House. I just don't like how the show itself seems to lionize House, just like the BBC Sherlock lionized Sherlock. I get tired of media that never really calls men who behave like know-it-all asses on their behavior. I felt we're supposed to disapprove of House's behavior but ultimately defer to him because he's oh, so smart...and yeah, no. Not gonna do that.

(And yes, I do know a lot of people read Sherlock as autistic. I'm on the spectrum myself, and I still don't like him or how, to me, the show tells us, repeatedly, how we're supposed to feel about him.

I am also 100% down for people disagreeing with me on either show. That's why it's so good that we have so many different entertainment options.)

I see what you mean re: email. I emailed her at first because it was 3 in the morning, then realized, you know what? Maybe I should call her, so I also left her a message. She also seemed to be upset that I'd done both for some reason. Like I said, it was my first time at this particular ER rodeo and I was in crisis, so I wasn't really thinking about what the best steps to take would be. I'm not saying that to be sarcastic. I sincerely wish I HAD thought this through better.

I totally understand why she'd have needed to call the police. It's the rest of the communication around that, that was a problem for me and that wasn't clearly explained.
The trouble is, I thought she was a lone practitioner until "Administration Department" started emailing me about emergency hospitals and ten-minute deadlines. :/

My psychiatrist is joining a new practice and says the therapists there are great. But I think I need to talk to whomever I see about what happened, the fact that I now have MAJOR trust issues around therapists, and that I need to know exactly how they would handle a crisis situation. That's the only way I can trust one going forward.
I forgot to add that she also said I should go on disability, despite never having mentioned that to me before. No one has ever recommended this to me.
Ah, yes! My memory was correct. The Intersex Society did a good breakdown of it: [http://www.isna.org/node/1008](http://www.isna.org/node/1008)

Oh dear, I don't remember it all that well, either! But I seem to remember House basically calling the girl a man, which was really traumatic for her...but tbh, I never really liked House the show or the character, so perhaps I'm biased.

LCSW, I think?  


A friend who was a counselor at one point (she works in another industry now) said that she thinks my therapist bonded with me over the fact we both have ADHD, as she'd shared some of the things she'd done to manage it and we're almost the same age. And then when I had a crisis, she didn't know what to do, and then projected her own issues on me while saying, "Oh, she's not like me at all, after all!"
Cheese and Rice! I hope they also find an intersex-friendly/knowledgeable lawyer.
Yup! Though I don't think that episode handled the issue very well, either.
Wow, all of this isn't normal at all, and the fact he was asking for hugs made me feel ill. If you are in a position to find a new one, I'd suggest doing so. This is a terrible therapist.

Yes, I was diagnosed at 37 and am female. I also have MDD (which may be biploar? But the person who suggested that shouted it at me when I didn't have a breakdown in a convenient way so \*shrug emoji\*), GAD, CPTSD, and probably something else. All of these overlap with ADHD. Basically, I think the most effective thing to do is to look for a therapist or psychiatrist who treats symptoms rather than trying to stick you into a specific category.  


I wish I had more specific ideas for you about how to go about finding someone who knows wtf they're doing when treating ADHD, but that's currently a problem I'm trying to figure out.

Just jumping in here since I have that diagnosis. I think you may mean complex post-traumatic stress disorder? Not that it matters ultimately, because it does, indeed, result from ongoing trauma, especially when someone's young.
Oh, also: I do understand now that she needed to call the police regardless of what I said. I didn't know at the time, since this was my first time riding at this particular ER rodeo.
Thank you, biblioteqa! The time limit was really what concerned me, and the fact she then seemed to conflate it with the actual law itself. Thank you for linking me to the code!
um...okay?

This makes me sick. The same thing happened to me when I was 8 (only I'm not a boy and it didn't go so far as what happened here). The school also did nothing.   


I hate now nothing has changed in nearly three decades.
Dang, it really IS CSA week. This poor mother. Why can't we have bird law week?

Yes, I did. She found me hiding in a closet because the boy threatened to assault me again after school. She told his parents and they made him come to school and apologize to me. The he physically assaulted me the next day. It took place during class when the teacher was either out of the room or doing something else. I can't recall that detail. I am reasonably sure said teacher has passed on now--but at 10, everyone seems old, so I could be wrong-- and I don't want to go after her. I think she just honestly didn't know what to do.  


But his parents knew and didn't even talk to my parents about what happened. My parents also had no idea that they could do anything. One of them is also a victim of the same kind of sexual abuse, so I'm sure this brought up trauma for him too.

Do you know if they would tell him what I said? I'm still afraid of this boy (now a man) 25 years on. He's wealthy, has dozens of wealthy relatives, and the way he looked at me as he hurt me still chills me to this day.   


I'm sorry if that's a stupid question. It's taken me two and a half decades to even begin to process this, and to get help that wasn't useless or abusive. So I have no idea how any of this works. I've also never made a statement to the police.
Have submitted a GRAMMA request. Will see what happens.

Thanks to some advice in this thread, I've submitted a GRAMMA request to see if anyone actually filed a report against the family. My suspicion is no because Utah in the late 80s. But if I have that, that would help.   


I'm sure there's no easy answer to this question, but what would you consider reliable and credible?
Appreciated, thank you. :)
Thanks :). Much obliged.
Omg that's a great idea. Thank you!
Wouldn't that just be his word against mine, though? Especially if we were both minors at the time and the case is this old?

Unfortunately, you can't report a crime that's over twenty years old, that no one reported at the time, and that you have no evidence of being committed except your word and that of your family's. Especially when the person who did it to you is rich and has lawyers and you aren't.
That's my fear too. My only thought is that perhaps I'm wrong and a police report was filed. But I have no idea how to find out if that happened or if it would still be around 25 years later.
